## Design: Two-Stage Miller Op-Amp with Cascoded NMOS First Stage

**Topology choice.** A plain two-stage Miller amplifier in sky130 gets roughly 80–85 dB, which is short of the 90 dB requirement. I add NMOS cascodes to the input pair and use long-L PMOS mirror loads, so the first-stage gain is set mostly by the PMOS load, gm1/gds4. That should give about 50–55 dB. A PMOS common-source second stage with long-L devices adds about 40 dB.

I did not cascode the PMOS side. The pfet |Vth| is about 1 V, so a PMOS cascode would not fit in 1.8 V.

The output stage is a single common-source stage, so the swing runs from about 0.2 V to about 1.6 V. That easily covers the 1 V requirement. The input pair is NMOS so it can take an input common-mode of 0.9 V.

**Operating point.** Expected DC voltages:
* **Tail node:** about 0.2–0.25 V.
* **Cascode bias (vcb):** about 1.0 V. It comes from a resistor feeding a diode-connected nfet, which costs about 5 µA.
* **First-stage output (out1):** about VDD − Vsg ≈ 0.7 V. This is also the right gate voltage for the PMOS M7.

**Polarity.** M2 (gate = vinp) drives out1. If vinp rises, out1 falls, so the PMOS second stage pushes vout up. That makes vinp the non-inverting input.

**Initial sizing and expected performance:**

| Quantity | Initial value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Tail current | 20 µA | |
| gm1 | ≈ 150 µS | gm/Id ≈ 15 |
| Compensation | Cc = 2 pF | |
| GBW | ≈ 12 MHz | gm1/(2π·Cc) |
| Second-stage current | ≈ 120 µA | |
| gm7 | ≈ 1.2 mS | needs > 2.2·gm1·CL/Cc ≈ 0.83 mS for 60° phase margin |
| Nulling resistor Rz | 2 kΩ | > 1/gm7, which moves the zero into the left half-plane |
| Slew rate | ≈ 10 V/µs | |
| Power | ≈ (10 + 20 + 120 + 5) µA × 1.8 V ≈ 280 µW | limit is 500 µW |

```spice
.subckt dut vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias
* ---- bias: reference sink and mirrors ----
MB0 ibias ibias vss vss nfet W=2 L={LB}
MT  tail  ibias vss vss nfet W={WT} L={LB}
M8  vout  ibias vss vss nfet W={W8} L={LB}
* ---- cascode gate bias (~1.0 V) ----
RCB vdd vcb {RCB}
MCB vcb vcb vss vss nfet W={WCB} L=4
* ---- first stage: NMOS diff pair + NMOS cascodes + PMOS mirror load ----
M1  n1   vinn tail vss nfet W={W1} L={L1}
M2  n2   vinp tail vss nfet W={W1} L={L1}
M1c d1   vcb  n1   vss nfet W={WC} L={LC}
M2c out1 vcb  n2   vss nfet W={WC} L={LC}
M3  d1   d1   vdd  vdd pfet W={W3} L={L3}
M4  out1 d1   vdd  vdd pfet W={W3} L={L3}
* ---- second stage: PMOS common source ----
M7  vout out1 vdd vdd pfet W={W7} L={L7}
* ---- Miller compensation with nulling resistor ----
RZ  out1 xc {RZ}
CC  xc   vout {CC}
.ends dut
```

```json
{"params": {
  "LB":  [1.5, 0.5, 4],
  "WT":  [4, 1, 12],
  "W8":  [24, 6, 80],
  "RCB": [160000, 60000, 400000],
  "WCB": [1, 0.42, 6],
  "W1":  [8, 2, 40],
  "L1":  [0.5, 0.25, 2],
  "WC":  [4, 1, 20],
  "LC":  [0.5, 0.25, 2],
  "W3":  [10, 2, 40],
  "L3":  [2, 0.5, 4],
  "W7":  [60, 10, 300],
  "L7":  [1, 0.5, 3],
  "RZ":  [2000, 200, 20000],
  "CC":  [2e-12, 0.5e-12, 5e-12]
}}
```

**Notes for the optimiser:**
* **Systematic offset.** This is lowest when (W7/L7)/(W3/L3) ≈ 2·I8/Itail. The DC servo in the testbench absorbs any offset that remains, but a large mismatch pushes M7 or M8 out of saturation.
* **vcb.** It must stay roughly in the 0.9–1.15 V range. That keeps both the tail and the input pair in saturation while leaving the cascode about 0.3 V of Vds. RCB and WCB set it.
* **Gain shortfall.** If gain falls short, increase L3, L7 and LB. If phase margin is short, increase W8 (more output current) or Cc, or adjust RZ.
